sourceText: cells: Bg, Ws The NIVEN-INTEGRAL sector was already in progress when they entered. For several lessons Aster had refused to pause worlds for their arrival; the fact that a class was visiting was not a cosmic event for the inhabitants. The children live inside a torus of gas where forests float and nothing has a stable “down.” The memorial bore the name of Larry Niven — The Integral Trees precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. In the worlds of this period, a single physical deviation had to be followed all the way through. If gravity changed, so did walking, the house, the weapon, the metaphor, the frontier, and the price of a life saved. Marae kept her local body vulnerable. Pain, fatigue, and the impossibility of doing ten things at once were epistemic instruments for her, not biological scenery. At the center of the conflict was En, an administrator chosen precisely because they were not a specialist in the phenomenon that had reorganized the world. ‘The specialists tell me what can be done,’ 71 they said. ‘I have to answer who it may be done to.’ Kesh kept the distinction in his notes. The problem closed quickly around them: A storm can be stopped, but the locals say that storms are precisely what redistribute life and fertility over the long term. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Bg — Biological Geography: the landscape itself is an organism or living process; Ws — World Ship: a ship is large enough to become a world. Course references included living-world traditions; generation-ship traditions. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Vela broke the first consensus. ‘If we can save the situation only by making the world resemble us more closely, we have not demonstrated the superiority of our solution. We have demonstrated only our power.’ Kesh answered without raising their voice: ‘If the element explains everything, we do not have an element. We have a word that has eaten the problem.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. The White Hunger appeared in Aster as a loss of relief. She did not lack entertainment. She lacked the resistance of things to the model. 72 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS When she could anticipate every reaction, the world became functionally an extension of her own mind, and the presence of the other thinned toward simulacrum. Vela evaluated the solution not by efficiency but by the differences it made invisible. She found one: a local minority for whom the proposed “improvement” destroyed a practice with no equivalent. Optimizing the average concealed a small and perfectly legal extinction. The night did not end in victory. Marae must accept a preventable loss and sees how easily a local rescue can destroy an ecosystem. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. Tern remained a few seconds after the others. A very faint deviation repeated in the sector’s background noise, too coherent to be thermal and too useless to be a teaching signal. He did not tell Aster. It was the first thing he possessed solely by not sharing it. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the EXTERNALIZATION operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — turns an internal property into an object, companion, infrastructure, or institution — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. 73 Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. They left without an oral summary. Aster had abandoned the habit of closing every night with a thesis; some worlds were more honestly preserved as problems than as lessons. 74 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
